---
title: "Desktop Visual Stacking & Unobstructed Key Provisioning Test"
description: "Verifies that the primary CTA is not occluded by floating overlays on 1920x1080 desktop"
tags: ["visual-assurance", "desktop", "stacking-context"]

# Desktop Stacking Occlusion Test

## 1. Open CloudScale Gateway
Open `http://localhost:3000/app` and wait for DOM hydration.

## 2. Verify Genesis State
Assert that the element with test ID `data-testid="key-status"` contains `SYSTEM_READY`.
Assert that the active key count element `data-testid="key-count"` displays `2 Keys`.

## 3. Provision Production Key
Click the button with test ID `data-testid="deploy-key-btn"`.

## 4. Confirm Successful Action Dispatch
Assert that the element with test ID `data-testid="key-status"` contains `KEY_GENERATED_HEALTHY`.
Assert that the key count element `data-testid="key-count"` now displays `3 Keys`.

Added the component and mounted it. Two notes on verification and one design call:

**Couldn't run checks** — `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run test:unit` both needed approval and were blocked, so the typecheck and unit suite are unrun. Everything below is from reading the code.

**What I built** — `app/app/CookieConsent.tsx:1`, mounted next to `MaintenanceNotice` in `app/app/CloudScaleDashboard.tsx:131`:

- First-time only: state starts `false` so SSR and the first client render agree (no hydration mismatch, no flash for returning visitors); a `useEffect` reveals the bar only when `localStorage` has no stored choice.
- Persists `"accepted"` / `"declined"` under `cloudscale.cookie-consent` (exported as `COOKIE_CONSENT_KEY`). Reads and writes are wrapped in try/catch — when storage is blocked it asks again next visit rather than assuming consent.
- CloudScale styling: `bg-white` / `border-cs-line` / `text-cs-sub`, brand-blue `Accept` matching `deploy-key-btn`, bordered white `Decline`, and `data-testid="cookie-consent" | "cookie-accept" | "cookie-decline"` so Kane objectives can drive it by test ID like the rest of the page.
- Uses `role="dialog"`, deliberately **not** `role="status"` — `tests/unit/cloudscale.test.tsx:75` does `screen.getByRole("status")`, which throws on multiple matches, so a second status role would have broken that test.

**The placement call:** it's a full-width bottom bar at `z-[60]`, above the maintenance toast's `z-50`. On a phone there's no overlap-free spot — the toast is already pinned full-width at the bottom — so while the bar is up it covers the toast's lower edge, and the toast is fully revealed once a choice is made. I put consent on top rather than underneath on purpose: the toast covering the consent buttons would be exactly the occlusion bug class this repo exists to catch. The Kane CTAs are unaffected (`deploy-key-btn` and `topup-btn` both sit well above the fold at 1920x1080 and at Kane's 800x1000 mobile window).

Worth knowing: with a fresh browser profile the bar now shows on every Kane run, so it's part of the demo app's first paint. If you'd rather the two never overlap, I can lift the consent state so `MaintenanceNotice` shifts up while the bar is visible — say the word and I'll wire it.
